A-PCRE-89156.conclusion: The proposed all-mode JIT workaround is not unconditional.
A-PCRE-89156.rationale: Qt requests all three modes and ignores the return value. PCRE2 10.47 installs modes successively and preserves earlier code when a later allocation fails. The bounded allocator probe retained complete-mode code after error -48, with both partial modes returning -45. Exact Mac x86_64 and Windows QtCore disassembly also ignores that result. The Mac arm64 slice has a no-JIT stub. The upstream advisory leaves 16-bit susceptibility unconfirmed; this probe proves partial compilation, not an out-of-bounds access or an app exploit.
evidenceNeededToResolve: Either rebuild with PCRE2 10.49 or its applicable fixes, or establish the exact 16-bit invalid-UTF/partial-match boundary including failed JIT compilation. A successful ordinary match is insufficient.
A-PCRE-89156.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-PCRE-89157.conclusion: Architecture and excluded conversion unit support non-applicability.
A-PCRE-89157.rationale: The advisory requires automatic pattern-conversion allocation with 32-bit size_t. Every inspected shipped image is 64-bit; Qt also omits pcre2_convert.c from its PCRE2 target. This is an architecture/API-specific conclusion for these bytes, not a claim that PCRE2 10.47 is fixed.
A-PCRE-89157.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-PCRE-89158.conclusion: The required 32-bit process and 32-bit code-unit API are absent.
A-PCRE-89158.rationale: Qt selects the 16-bit code-unit library. Mac x86_64/arm64 and Windows AMD64 use 64-bit processes. The advisory requires pcre2_compile_32 in a 32-bit process. The observed build and architectures exclude both prerequisites.
A-PCRE-89158.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-PCRE-89160.conclusion: The necessary invalid-UTF compile flag is absent from the traced Qt interface.
A-PCRE-89160.rationale: QRegularExpression maps its finite PatternOptions and adds PCRE2_UTF, but never PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF (0x04000000). Matching options do not add it either. The compiled Mac x86_64 and Windows option masks agree with this mapping. The PCRE2 compiler has no pattern-start verb that enables this flag. The 16-bit width alone would not exclude this advisory.
A-PCRE-89160.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-PCRE-89161.conclusion: Copied-subject reuse is absent from the traced Qt path.
A-PCRE-89161.rationale: Qt allocates fresh match data for doMatch, never sets COPY_MATCHED_SUBJECT, and calls pcre2_match_16. That wrapper clears any copied-subject flag before its internal JIT dispatch. Internal JIT execution is therefore not mistaken for a direct-API reuse call. No other first-party or Qt consumer of the affected direct API was found.
A-PCRE-89161.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-PCRE-89162.conclusion: The affected bytecode serialization API has no traced consumer.
A-PCRE-89162.rationale: pcre2_serialize.c is a Qt target input, so absence of code is not claimed. The complete Qt and first-party consumer search found no call to pcre2_serialize_encode. Qt serializes QRegularExpression pattern text/options instead. PCRE2 symbols are private in the inspected QtCore interfaces. The conclusion is limited to this closed packaged composition.
A-PCRE-89162.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

A-APPLE-27171.conclusion: No established vendor patch mapping across the supported OS baseline.
A-APPLE-27171.rationale: The system loader identity is confirmed, but Apple ABI version 1.2.12 cannot establish inclusion of the negative-length CRC fix ba829a458576d1ff0f26fc7230c6de816d1f6a77. These observations narrow the path but do not prove every alias/internal consumer or macOS 13+ runtime fixed.

A-PCRE-DFA.conclusion: DFA API is not used by the traced packaged consumers.
A-PCRE-DFA.rationale: The advisory affects pcre2_dfa_match with recursive workspace reuse and a low heap limit. No conclusion is inferred from its absence in Grype.

A-PCRE-STACK.conclusion: Affected JIT-stack mechanism is present on x86_64; app exploitability is not established.
A-PCRE-STACK.rationale: Qt assigns a JIT-stack callback and creates a 32–512 KiB growable stack after STACKLIMIT. The 10.49 advisory covers this 16-bit path. The Mac arm64 no-JIT stub excludes that slice; native Mac x86_64 and Windows x64 require further analysis. First-party expressions found are fixed; source-search uses RE2; KSyntaxHighlighting disables standard paths and escapes dynamic captures. Those are meaningful restrictions, but a complete bounded-pattern audit of all reachable Qt/KSyntax consumers was not established. Use PCRE2 10.49 as the forward remediation target; no app exploit is claimed.
evidenceNeededToResolve: Qualify a PCRE2 10.49/fixed-backport producer, or demonstrate and have the security owner accept a complete pattern-origin/complexity boundary for every JIT-enabled packaged consumer.
A-PCRE-STACK.expiryOrRecheckCondition: Recheck before the next release, on any artifact/source/dependency/build-option/architecture/OS-baseline/advisory-feed change, or by 2026-11-15, whichever occurs first. This technical review grants no security-owner waiver.

disagreements.claim: Requesting all JIT modes establishes the documented workaround for CVE-2026-89156.
disagreements.result: Not established under partial JIT compilation failure. The source probe is a concrete counterexample to that invariant; exact x86_64 binaries ignore the result.
Confirmed open applicability gap: the affected Qt growable-stack mechanism is present on x86_64, with meaningful but incomplete pattern-trust restrictions. 10.49 is the appropriate forward target.

E-INPUTS.observation: All 14 retained release assets plus both raw reports match their recorded SHA-256. Frozen summary hashes match. Queue-to-raw multiset equality is exact: 33 Mac and 31 Windows rows. Both binding verifiers retain exit 2.

E-MAC-INVENTORY.observation: 44 SPDX file hashes match the extracted app (following in-bundle symlinks). All 39 regular non-AppleDouble ZIP files match the extraction. ZIP has 181 entries and zero .jar/.class/.war/.ear files. Fourteen real Mach-O images, each with x86_64 and arm64 slices, were inspected. No bundled JVM or libdbus implementation appears in the payload.

fileVerification.excludedFromZipFileCompare: directories, symlink records and AppleDouble metadata

E-WIN-INVENTORY.observation: Extracted the MSI OLE cabinet stream, then decompressed it with cabextract. All 24 SPDX-listed files match exact SHA-256; the 25th cabinet member is the SBOM itself. All 17 PE images are AMD64 (0x8664). Runtime-ZIP Qt and main executable bytes also match. Cabinet has no Java archive/class payload or JVM; no gzwrite/gzprintf/gzvprintf/gzclose or PCRE2 import/export was found.

fileVerification.extraction: OLE stream extraction using olefile, then cabextract; direct cabextract-on-MSI failed and its outputs were excluded.

E-WIN-INVENTORY.scope: Read-only cabinet inspection on macOS, not Windows installation, Authenticode verification or native runtime execution.

E-PCRE-SOURCE.observation: Both corresponding-source assets contain byte-identical QtBase 6.11.2. PCRE2 header is 10.47, date 2025-10-21. Target sets PCRE2_CODE_UNIT_WIDTH=16, omits conversion, includes DFA/serialize/JIT source, and disables JIT for Apple arm64. qregularexpression.cpp lines 669-706/896-906 map flags, 1001-1011 ignore JIT result, 1056-1073 allocate/retry a growable stack, and 1148-1150 allocate fresh match data.

E-PCRE-BINARY.observation: Exact package QtCore interfaces contain no public pcre2 symbols. Focused disassembly corroborates the source option mapping and ignored JIT result in both x86_64 producers. Mac arm64 JIT call target is a no-JIT stub.
E-PCRE-BINARY.scope: Focused code-path corroboration, not complete disassembly, native Intel/Windows execution, or proof of dead-stripped code absence.

E-JIT-PROBE.output: PARTIAL_JIT_RETAINED failure_allocation=6 jit_result=-48 complete=1 partial_soft=-45 partial_hard=-45
E-JIT-PROBE.scope: Pinned Qt source compiled as a disposable JIT-enabled 16-bit PCRE2 harness on arm64; not execution of shipped Qt or native Windows/Intel evidence.
E-JIT-PROBE.reproduction: Save sourceCode as jit-partial-probe.c. Extract the hash-verified QtBase archive. Compile it with every .c unit listed in src/3rdparty/pcre2/CMakeLists.txt, -O1 -DHAVE_CONFIG_H -DPCRE2_CODE_UNIT_WIDTH=16 and that directory/src as the include path. Do not add PCRE2_DISABLE_JIT for this source-semantics probe. Execute with a 15-second process timeout. Never treat this JIT-enabled arm64 harness as the shipped arm64 Qt build.

E-CONSUMERS.observation: Exact git revisions each have QRegularExpression uses only in github_capability_probe.cpp and feedback_label_controls.cpp; these patterns are fixed. No direct PCRE2 calls were found in first-party src. Qt src outside its third-party implementation has one PCRE2 consumer: qregularexpression.cpp. KSyntaxHighlighting rule.cpp uses the Qt interface, NormalMatch and escaped dynamic captures (lines 89-94, 613-618, 687-697). The exact first-party syntax provider sets NO_STANDARD_PATHS=ON at line 519, and packaged_definition_catalog adds no custom path. The packaged source-search engine is RE2. These observations do not complete every Qt internal pattern-origin/complexity proof.

E-TIKA.observation: Both SPDX PURLs end with #tika-core/src/main/resources/org/apache/tika/mime/tika-mimetypes.xml at commit c29724782854bb5a319f4a1940d0828a58ace3f9. Qt attribution Files contains only tika-mimetypes.xml; mimetypes_resources.cmake packages it under /qt-project.org/qmime/tika/packages. Apache CNA descriptions were independently read for all eleven post-2016 entries; the 2016 MITRE record and Apache security table corroborate JMatIO/MATLAB. No executable Tika handler is represented by this resource.
E-TIKA.warning: Apache security.html labels one standards-handler entry CVE-2022-30216; the CNA record explicitly identifies this queue row as CVE-2022-30126. The queue ID was preserved.

E-SQLITE.observation: Both supplied source archives contain this same amalgamation. Header SQLITE_VERSION is 3.53.4 and SQLITE_VERSION_NUMBER is 3053004. Full SOURCE_ID is found twice in the universal app and once in the MSI executable. Raw Bitnami constraints were individually read and are unbounded above, with no fixed-version metadata.

E-NATIVE-ZLIB.observation: First-party SPDXRef-zlib uses the native madler archive and the same six-file provider on both revisions (adler32, crc32, inffast, inflate, inftrees, zutil), excluding all gz I/O. Qt BundledZLIB includes gzwrite.c; its failed-gz_comp branch at lines 245-246 returns without resetting avail_in/next_in, unlike the upstream fix. Gui/Network attributions point to that same 1.3.2 input; they are not three independently verified vulnerable call paths.

E-DBUS.observation: Qt attribution points to dbus_minimal_p.h. qdbus_symbols.cpp lazily attempts libdbus-1 versions 3, 2 and unversioned; a successful load must resolve dbus_connection_open_private. No libdbus implementation is bundled. Neither absence of direct Mach-O libdbus imports nor a standalone failed loader attempt establishes an active application-wide runtime exclusion.

E-APPLE-ZLIB.observation: otool -L reports /usr/lib/libz.1.dylib in both exact QtCore slices, ABI current version 1.2.12. otool -l shows LC_BUILD_VERSION minos 13.0 for both main-app and QtCore slices. None of the 28 inspected Mach-O slices imports inflateGetHeader or any crc32_combine-family symbol. Qt C++ and LibArchive source searches found no such calls. Vendor OS patch identity is separate from ABI identity.

E-RUNTIME.scope: Standalone loader/API probes; x86_64 runs under Rosetta, not native Intel; no app session or bus connection was started.
E-RUNTIME.reproduction: Compile the included source twice with clang -arch arm64 and clang -arch x86_64. Invoke each with zlib and dbus, with a three-second subprocess timeout. This probes system loading without opening a bus connection or an application window.
